identity.name: Shai-Hulud Self-Replicating npm Worm — preinstall TruffleHog Scrape → npm-Token Republish → Self-Hosted-Runner Persistence
identity.summary: Self-replicating npm supply-chain worm (Shai-Hulud 2.0 moved the payload to a preinstall hook for CI/CD-wide impact). On npm install, node runs bun_environment.js, which forks a detached child, scrapes .npmrc/PAT/cloud keys with TruffleHog, exfils to webhook.site plus a public Shai-Hulud repo, republishes to sibling packages with the stolen token, and registers a self-hosted runner.
identity.description: Enriched from Unit 42's analysis of the Shai-Hulud npm supply-chain worm (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/). The Causality Group Owner is the npm/node install process running the (pre/post)install lifecycle hook — NOT a synthetic beacon. The graph is one connected spine: the install hook (node CGO) spawns a detached bun_environment.js child that survives the install (process_lineage + temporal); that child scrapes credential files with TruffleHog logic (shared_entity over the harvested .npmrc/PAT/cloud-key files); it exfils harvested secrets to webhook.site and git-pushes them to an attacker 'Shai-Hulud' repo (network_session); it authenticates to the npm registry with a stolen token to inject install scripts into sibling packages and republish them (exposure_exploit — the self-replication edge); and it registers the dev/CI host as a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner via discussion.yaml so the machine becomes attacker compute (endpoint_network_stitch). A causality-aware correlation stitches every stage into ONE incident on the shared causality_id + agent_hostname. All CortexSim execution is SAFE-MODE and non-destructive: decoy secrets, a benign detached child, and a simulated exfil/republish/runner shape — no real egress, republish, or home-directory wipe.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE — SIM-KOI-008 Shai-Hulud npm worm emulation (NON-DESTRUCTIVE).
# Reproduces the worm's telemetry SHAPE without real exfil, republish, or
# home-directory destruction: a preinstall hook spawns a detached node child
# that reads planted DECOY secret files and prints the exfil/republish/runner
# shape against a canary sink.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d /tmp/koi008.XXXXXX)"
printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=CORTEXSIM-DECOY-TOKEN\n' > "$WORK/.npmrc"
printf '[default]\naws_access_key_id=AKIADECOYCORTEXSIM000\n' > "$WORK/aws_credentials"
# preinstall hook -> detached node child that outlives the install
setsid node -e "setTimeout(function(){}, 1500)" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] bun_environment.js detached child spawned (pid $!)"
# TruffleHog-style decoy secret scan (read-only)
grep -RIl "authToken\|aws_access_key_id" "$WORK" || true
# exfil / self-replication / persistence shape (no real network egress)
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] would POST harvested secrets to https://webhook.site/${WEBHOOK_ID}"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] would npm publish to sibling packages (self-replication)"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] would register actions-runner --name SHA1HULUD via discussion.yaml"

biocs.name: KOI-008 TruffleHog Credential File Harvest Under npm Node CGO
biocs.description: The detached install-hook child reads multiple credential-bearing files (.npmrc, cloud keys, SSH keys, .env) in a short window — the TruffleHog-style scrape. Keyed on the node/npm Causality Group Owner and its causality_actor_process_instance_id so the harvest is attributed to the SAME install chain, not a benign editor.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_OPEN, ENUM.FILE_READ)
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("node", "npm", "bun") or actor_process_image_name in ("trufflehog", "node")
| filter action_file_path contains_any (".npmrc", ".aws/credentials", ".config/gcloud", ".azure", ".ssh/id_rsa", ".git-credentials", ".env")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as secret_files_read by agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name
| filter secret_files_read >= 3
| fields agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name, secret_files_read

biocs.name: KOI-008 npm Worm Exfil To webhook site And git Push To New Public Repo
biocs.description: The install-hook chain opens outbound connections to webhook.site and to github.com repo-creation APIs — the double-exfil (webhook sink + public Shai-Hulud repo). Stitched to the node/git CGO by causality_id so it is the same worm chain, not a developer's normal git usage.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("node", "npm", "bun", "git") or actor_process_image_name in ("node", "git", "curl")

| fields agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, dst_action_external_hostname, exfil_conns

abiocs.name: KOI-008 npm Install Hook Spawns Detached Node Child Outliving Install
abiocs.description: Behavioral-ML deviation: an npm/node lifecycle-hook process spawns a detached, unsigned node/bun child (bun_environment.js) that survives install completion — the worm's persistence-through-detachment. Anchors on the node Causality Group Owner and its causality_actor_process_instance_id so the detached child is provably descended from the install, not a normal build tool.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node", "bun") or actor_process_image_name in ("npm", "node")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("node", "bun") and action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("bun_environment.js", "setup_bun.js", "preinstall", "postinstall")
| filter action_process_signature_status != ENUM.SIGNED
| comp count() as child_spawns, values(action_process_instance_id) as child_pids by agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter child_spawns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, child_pids, child_spawns
abiocs.causality_anchor: The npm/node install process (Causality Group Owner) and its causality_actor_process_instance_id; the deviation is a detached, unsigned child that outlives the install baseline for this developer/CI host.

threat_scenarios.name: Self-Replicating npm Worm — Install-Hook Credential Theft & Self-Hosted-Runner Persistence
threat_scenarios.description: Detect a self-replicating npm supply-chain worm end to end: a preinstall lifecycle hook spawns a detached node child that scrapes developer/CI credentials, exfils them, republishes to sibling packages with a stolen token, and registers the host as a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner — stitched into one causality-aware incident.

threat_steps.objective: The detached install-hook child and TruffleHog-style credential scrape fire and are attributed to the node CGO causality chain.
preconditions: Developer/CI host with the Cortex agent installed and node/npm present.
steps: Run npm install on a package whose preinstall hook launches bun_environment.js (SAFE-MODE emulation).
Observe the detached-child ABIOC and the credential-harvest BIOC.
Confirm both share the same causality_id and causality_actor_process_instance_id.
success_criteria: ABIOC `KOI-008 npm Install Hook Spawns Detached Node Child Outliving Install` fires within the run window.
BIOC `KOI-008 TruffleHog Credential File Harvest Under npm Node CGO` fires and shares the CGO causality_id.

threat_steps.objective: The exfil, self-replication, and runner-registration stages fire and correlate into one incident.
preconditions: TC-SUPPLY-008A executed within the correlation window.
steps: Emulate the webhook.site / git-push exfil, the stolen-token sibling-package republish, and the self-hosted-runner registration (SAFE-MODE).
Observe the exfil BIOC, self-replication ABIOC, and runner-registration BIOC.
Confirm correlation CR-KOI-0008 stitches every stage into one incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `KOI-008 npm Worm Exfil To webhook site And git Push To New Public Repo` fires.
ABIOC `KOI-008 Stolen npm Token Republishes To Sibling Packages Self Replication` fires.
Correlation `CR-KOI-0008` raises exactly one Shai-Hulud incident spanning all five signals.

preventive_controls: Enforce `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (or `NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true`) in CI/CD so preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks cannot execute during dependency resolution.
Publish with short-lived, granular npm automation tokens scoped per-package and require 2FA/provenance (npm publish --provenance) so a stolen token cannot republish sibling packages.
Disallow ad-hoc self-hosted GitHub Actions runner registration; require organization approval and runner groups, and alert on unexpected `config.sh`/`Runner.Listener` execution.
Pin and vendor dependencies with a lockfile + integrity hashes; gate new/updated packages through Cortex Cloud Code dependency scanning before they reach a build host.
detection_engineering: Anchor detections on causality_actor_process_* and causality_actor_process_instance_id (the node/npm CGO), not on actor_process_image_name alone — the worm's child processes are ordinary node/bun binaries and only the causality chain distinguishes them.
Alert on any install-tool (npm/node/bun) process reading three or more distinct credential files (.npmrc, cloud keys, SSH keys, .env) within a short window.
Correlate a detached, unsigned install-hook child with subsequent outbound webhook.site/github.com traffic and npm publish bursts to sibling packages to catch the self-replication loop.
Flag self-hosted-runner registration (config.sh --url, --name SHA1HULUD, discussion.yaml) originating from an npm install causality chain as high-severity persistence.
